source.topic: Mike Tyson's boxing life: discipline, championship, adversity, and reinvention
source.source_text: FACT RECORD — Tyson’s life and boxing career. Born in Brooklyn, New York, on June 30, 1966. As a teenager, met Bobby Stewart, a counselor and former boxer; Stewart introduced Tyson to trainer Cus D’Amato. D’Amato later served as Tyson’s coach and legal guardian. Tyson won Junior Olympic gold medals in 1981 and 1982. Professional debut: March 6, 1985. First 19 professional bouts: knockout victories. D’Amato died November 4, 1985, before Tyson won a world heavyweight title. On November 22, 1986, Tyson defeated Trevor Berbick for the WBC heavyweight title at age 20, becoming boxing’s youngest heavyweight champion at the time. In 1987 Tyson won the WBA heavyweight title, then defeated Tony Tucker to unify WBC, WBA, and IBF heavyweight titles. His first professional loss was to James “Buster” Douglas in Tokyo in 1990. In 1992 Tyson was convicted of rape in Indiana and sentenced to prison; he was released on parole in 1995. He returned to boxing, regained the WBC and WBA titles in 1996, and later that year lost the WBA title to Evander Holyfield. In their 1997 rematch Tyson was disqualified after biting Holyfield’s ears; Nevada’s commission revoked his boxing license and later restored it. Lennox Lewis knocked Tyson out in 2002. Reported end-of-2005 record: 50 wins, 6 losses, 2 no contests, 44 knockouts. Muhammad Ali, Sugar Ray Robinson, and Joe Frazier are contextual historical figures only, not Tyson’s opponents or coaches.
